title: TCSA-UDA: Text-driven cross-semantic alignment for unsupervised domain adaptation in medical image segmentation
abstract: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for medical image segmentation remains challenging due to substantial domain shifts across imaging modalities, such as CT and MRI. Although recent vision-language representation learning methods have shown promise in medical image analysis, their role in cross-modality UDA segmentation remains underexplored. To address this problem, we propose TCSA-UDA, a Text-driven Cross-Semantic Alignment framework that uses modality-aware textual prompting to guide domain-invariant visual representation learning. Specifically, we introduce a vision-language covariance cosine loss (VLCoL) that aligns inter-class visual feature relationships with text-derived semantic relationships, encouraging the image encoder to learn semantically structured and modality-robust representations. In addition, we incorporate a prototype alignment module to reduce residual class-level discrepancies between source and target domains by aligning high-level class prototypes. Extensive experiments on cross-modality cardiac, abdominal, and brain tumor segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that TCSA-UDA consistently improves adaptation performance and outperforms state-of-the-art UDA methods. These results highlight the potential of language-driven semantic guidance for domain-adaptive medical image segmentation. The code is available at https://github.com/lalitmaurya47/TCSA_UDA

title: A comprehensive review of one-pixel attack: Research status, taxonomy, applications, regulation policy, and future directions
abstract: One-Pixel Attacks (OPAs) represent one of the most extreme demonstrations of adversarial fragility in deep learning, where modifying a single pixel can reliably induce high-confidence misclassification across domains such as medical diagnosis, autonomous driving, biometrics, and quantum communication. Despite their conceptual simplicity, OPAs remain underexamined in existing adversarial-attack surveys, which provide only fragmented or cursory coverage. This PRISMA-guided review synthesizes high-quality studies from 2017 to 2026 and delivers a unified, multi-axis taxonomy of OPA research spanning algorithmic foundations, black-box evolutionary optimization, emerging hybrid and program-synthesis attacks, defence mechanisms, interpretability tools, and domain-specific vulnerabilities. Our analysis reveals the dominance of Differential Evolution-based strategies, the rise of efficiency-optimized and saliency-guided methods, and persistent gaps in dataset diversity, transferability, and standardized evaluation. We summarized and assess defence paradigms including pixel restoration, anomaly detection, input-space transformations, and robust training highlighting their trade-offs in robustness, imperceptibility, and computational overhead. Building on these insights, we outline future research priorities involving selective pixel recovery, transformer-specific vulnerability analysis, saliency-driven optimization, and real-world domain-adaptive defences. We further propose a regulatory framework emphasizing robustness testing, incident disclosure, and AI security governance. This review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding, evaluating, and mitigating ultra-sparse adversarial threats in contemporary AI systems.

title: DABP: Dual-augmented budgeted channel pruning via sensitivity-aware gating
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) achieve strong performance across a wide range of computer vision tasks but remain computationally demanding for resource-constrained devices. Structured channel pruning reduces model complexity by removing redundant channels and filters; however, existing methods often rely on heuristic or computationally expensive strategies, lack precise control over compression, and struggle to preserve performance during training.In this work, we propose Dual-Augmented Budgeted Pruning (DABP), a differentiable channel pruning framework that formulates network compression as a budget-constrained optimization problem. The proposed method introduces continuous channel-wise gating variables and integrates an augmented Lagrangian mechanism to explicitly enforce a global resource budget during training. Additionally, a sensitivity-aware regularization term, derived from gradient-based statistics, is employed to preserve informative feature representations. Unlike sparsity-based or fixed-penalty methods that achieve the target compression level indirectly through regularization strength and threshold selection, DABP explicitly steers the optimization toward a predefined global resource budget via online dual-variable updates. Meanwhile, the sensitivity-aware regularization complements this process by discouraging the removal of highly informative channels, enabling accurate budget control while maintaining predictive performance under aggressive compression.Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet demonstrate that DABP achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, outperforming several state-of-the-art structured pruning methods. In particular, on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-56, DABP achieves 93.76% Top-1 accuracy with a significant reduction in FLOPs (54.56%). On ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012), it achieves up to 75.56% Top-1 accuracy with a 56.66% reduction in FLOPs, demonstrating its effectiveness under both moderate and high compression rates.

title: FedAntiDiaPep: Privacy-preserving deep learning framework for antidiabetic peptides identification using federated learning
abstract: Diabetes is one of the most common chronic ailments in the world, resulting in an increase in patients needing effective treatment. Anti-diabetic peptides are promising candidates for the treatment of diabetes since they can influence glucose metabolism. This study presents a novel federated deep learning framework called FedAntiDiaPed for Anti-diabetic peptide identification. This framework combines advanced feature engineering, hybrid deep learning, and federated learning to ensure data security. FedAntiDiaPed uses a hybrid model of feature engineering that combines Quasi-Sequence Order (QSO) and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA). QSO is used to extract sequence-order and physicochemical features, and LSA captures latent contextual features of the peptides. The hybrid architecture adopts the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)– Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU) method for processing the extracted features. The CNNs segment analysis analyzes the local sequences and recognizes the patterns of the extracted features. BiGRU captures the long-range dependencies and the bidirectional contextual information of the sequences. Thus, it becomes possible for FedAntiDiaPed to learn different aspects of the peptide sequences. The experiments conducted reveal that the proposed hybrid model is very efficient in operation. So far, FedAntiDiaPed has achieved an accuracy of 0.9776 with an MCC of 0.9553, making it more efficient than the existing models currently in use. The results show how the combination of various technologies has worked in favor of the hybrid model. All in all, it can be said that FedAntiDiaPed is an efficient and effective method for the identification of Anti-diabetic peptides. The use of federated learning empowers the technology to carry out model training without data sharing. Thus, the process proves to be useful in the field of drug development and in creating personalized diabetes treatment plans while ensuring data privacy.

title: Hierarchical Laplacian convolutional neural solver for nonlinear mechanical response prediction
abstract: This paper presents a Hierarchical Laplacian Convolutional Neural Solver (HL-CNS), a physics-guided neural multigrid framework for predicting nonlinear mechanical responses. The proposed approach embeds the error-correction pathway of a multigrid V-cycle directly into a learnable neural architecture, while representing the underlying differential operator through a data-adaptive Laplacian kernel. Residual-based neural networks are used to model solution updates, replacing conventional iterative smoothers with learned corrections. The framework is evaluated on 2-D and 3-D thermal diffusion problems with temperature-dependent conductivity, as well as 3-D linear elasticity and bilinear elasto-plasticity. Across these benchmarks, HL-CNS achieves accurate and consistent predictions in both linear and nonlinear regimes, and compares favorably with representative neural architectures, including ResNet, FCN, U-Net, and DeepONet. In nonlinear elasto-plastic cases, HL-CNS reduces inference cost by several orders of magnitude relative to conventional finite-element solvers, as predictions are obtained through a single fixed-depth forward pass without requiring iterative constitutive updates. These results demonstrate that embedding multigrid-inspired hierarchical structure and residual-based correction into neural architecture provides an effective and scalable approach for surrogate modeling of complex PDE systems. The proposed framework is particularly well-suited for many-query scenarios, such as parametric analysis, uncertainty quantification, and real-time prediction, where fixed-cost inference is critical.

title: A survey on heterogeneous image domain adaptation
abstract: Supervised deep learning usually requires large amounts of labelled data, which is often difficult to obtain. Domain adaptation alleviates this by transferring knowledge from one labelled dataset to another (either unlabelled or partially labelled), and heterogeneous domain adaptation (HDA) is particularly challenging because the domains lie in different spaces. It is an emerging field of research, encompassing diverse backgrounds and fields that use a variety of sensors (remote sensing, robotics, etc.), and thus a review of HDA approaches is necessary to provide a global view and showcase recent developments. As such, this survey provides a comprehensive overview of current heterogeneous image domain adaptation methods, inspecting their capabilities and limitations, and elucidating future research directions. It focuses on works that consider image modalities of different dimensionality, since this is rarely addressed. The survey proposes a feature-based categorisation of HDA methods based on the feature space in which DA is performed. This article also provides an overview of HDA applications and benchmark datasets, and gives recommendations on their proper use. Finally, the article’s discussion offers concrete guidance and advice for end-users and researchers.

title: Context-aware hierarchical GNN with temporal-decay graph diffusion for dynamic graph anomaly detection
Hybrid dynamic modeling based on data-driven physical iterative and physics-informed neural networks for UAV systems
Learning Alzheimer’s disease signatures by bridging EEG with spiking neural networks and biophysical simulations
abstract: As the prevalence of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) increases, there is a growing need for interpretable biomarkers derived from non-invasive neural recordings. While deep learning approaches applied to electroencephalography (EEG) achieve strong classification performance, they often lack mechanistic interpretability and require large datasets. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide a biologically grounded alternative, yet their relationship to large-scale brain dynamics remains insufficiently understood, and their potential for low-power deployment on neuromorphic hardware remains largely unquantified in this domain. We propose a conceptual framework in which data-driven models and mechanistic simulations are linked through convergence on a common physiological axis, namely the excitation–inhibition (E/I) balance. Within this framework, EEG-derived functional connectivity, estimated using network-based statistics, is used as a connectivity prior to constrain large-scale spiking network simulations, enabling empirically informed circuit dynamics. In parallel, an SNN classifier trained on resting-state EEG achieves competitive performance (AUC = 0.804–0.844), with the aperiodic 1/f slope emerging as a discriminative marker corresponding to E/I imbalance, creating a further conceptual bridge. Deployed on SpiNNaker neuromorphic hardware, the latency-encoded SNN retains competitive classification performance (AUC = 0.793–0.839) while reducing estimated energy consumption per inference to approximately one third of a GPU-based baseline on SpiNNaker 2, demonstrating the practical viability of low-power neuromorphic deployment for this task. To mechanistically interpret the EEG findings, we simulate spiking networks with systematically varied inhibitory-to-excitatory ratios under both unconstrained and connectivity-constrained conditions. The resulting dynamics reproduce key spectral features of empirical EEG, including spectral slowing and alpha-band modulation, with functional connectivity priors improving alignment between simulated and observed spectral structure. Overall, by grounding both machine learning and biophysical simulations in a shared E/I balance framework, constraining circuit dynamics with empirical connectivity, and validating low-power deployment on neuromorphic hardware, this work provides a coherent, interpretable, and practically deployable account of EEG biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease.

title: From brain to intervention: A framework for real-time stress detection using OpenBCI and machine learning
DecNefSimulator: A modular, interpretable framework for decoded neurofeedback simulation using generative models
abstract: Decoded Neurofeedback (DecNef) is a promising non-invasive approach to brain modulation with wide-ranging applications in neuromedicine and cognitive neuroscience. However, progress in DecNef research remains constrained by subject-dependent learning variability, reliance on indirect measures to quantify progress, and the high cost and time demands of experimentation. We present DecNefSimulator, a modular and interpretable simulation framework that formalizes DecNef as a machine learning problem. Beyond providing a virtual laboratory, DecNefSimulator enables researchers to model, analyze and understand neurofeedback dynamics. Using latent variable generative models as simulated participants, DecNefSimulator allows direct observation of internal cognitive states and systematic evaluation of how different protocol designs and subject characteristics influence learning. We demonstrate how this approach can (i) reproduce empirical phenomena of DecNef learning, (ii) identify conditions under which DecNef feedback fails to induce learning, and (iii) guide the design of more robust and reliable DecNef protocols in silico before human implementation. In summary, DecNefSimulator bridges computational modeling and cognitive neuroscience, offering a principled foundation for methodological innovation, robust protocol design, and ultimately, a deeper understanding of DecNef-based brain modulation.

title: Second-order predefined-time neural networks for sparse recovery
abstract: Sparse signal recovery from limited linear measurements is a fundamental problem in compressive sensing and related inverse problems. It remains challenging due to its combinatorial nature and the lack of algorithms with guaranteed or explicitly controllable convergence times. In order to deal with this issue, in this paper, we study the continuous time neural dynamic approaches for solving the l0-norm sparse recovery problem. First, by modifying the WBP function, we give a smoothing approximation of the l0-norm, and then develop a convex relaxation of the sparse optimization problem. Second, by introducing the sliding technique, we propose a second-order time-varying predefined-time neurodynamic approach. And then we give some theoretical analysis, such as model equivalence, solution existence and predefined-time convergence. Third, a discrete-time counterpart of the proposed neural network is further derived, which is shown to inherit the predefined-time convergence in the sense of discrete time. Moreover, we develop a delayed second-order neurodynamic system and investigate its asymptotic stability. Finally, numerical experiments on sparse recovery and feature selection demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: RS-OVD: Region-semantic stabilization for open-vocabulary object detection
abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) aims to localize and recognize objects described by arbitrary category names, including classes that are not annotated during detector training. Despite the progress achieved by vision-language pretraining, existing OVD methods still face three practical challenges: unstable region-level semantic alignment, high-confidence false positives from semantically similar backgrounds, and performance degradation when new categories are introduced incrementally. To address these issues, this paper proposes RS-OVD, a region-semantic stabilization framework for robust open-vocabulary detection under both static and dynamically expanding vocabularies. The proposed method learns a unified region embedding space in which object queries are aligned with category semantics while preserving local visual discrimination. To strengthen positive region representation, RS-OVD integrates category-level textual guidance, cropped-object semantic consistency, and region-level structural constraints into the training objective. To refine the negative decision boundary, a margin-based hard negative suppression strategy is designed to identify background proposals with low spatial overlap but high semantic similarity to category prototypes, thereby reducing high-confidence false detections caused by contextual or visually similar regions. Furthermore, for incremental open-world scenarios, memory replay and parameter stabilization are incorporated to maintain old-category knowledge while adapting to newly added categories with limited annotations. Extensive experiments on COCO and LVIS demonstrate that RS-OVD improves seen-category detection, novel-category generalization, rare-category robustness, and continual adaptation. On COCO, RS-OVD achieves 60.4 Seen AP, 42.3 Novel AP, 58.6 AP50, and 47.6 AP75, showing stronger generalization to held-out categories while preserving accurate object localization. On LVIS, it obtains 35.8 AP and 26.2 APr, with consistent gains across common and frequent categories, indicating improved robustness under large-vocabulary and long-tailed conditions. These results suggest that explicitly stabilizing region-semantic representations and suppressing semantically similar background responses provide an effective route for reliable open-vocabulary object detection. Code and models are available at https://github.com/1colorworker/RS-OVD.git.
